title: 5 Kinds of Reaction Heat Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A gas flame gives heat out, a cold pack takes heat in, and pulling a Lego tower apart takes effort. Every change has its own heat story. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 5, Thermodynamics) Diya lights the gas stove and we ask how chemists name and measure each kind of heat change.

You will see the standard state (pure, 1 bar, usually 298 K) and the standard enthalpy of reaction, then watch one mole of water being built from its elements on the molecule bench (formation, -285.8 kJ/mol; elements in their normal form are 0) and methane being pulled apart bond by bond (atomization, +1665 kJ/mol; mean C-H bond enthalpy 416). Combustion (butane -2658, glucose -2802) and enthalpy of solution for salt (+788 - 784 = +4 kJ/mol) follow, with neutralisation for ISC students. We derive products minus reactants step by step on the limestone example (+178.3 kJ), work out H2 + Cl2 -> 2HCl from bond enthalpies (-185 kJ), show the sign trap, then an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 54 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

In this video:
0:00 Every change has a heat story
0:25 Standard state and standard enthalpy of reaction
0:44 Enthalpy of formation: building water
1:18 Atomization and bond enthalpy: pulling methane apart
1:52 Combustion and enthalpy of solution
2:22 Pause and think: is -92.4 the formation value of NH3?
2:48 Products minus reactants, step by step
3:26 Worked example: bond enthalpies for HCl
3:57 Exam trap: the wrong subtraction
4:16 Practice question (NEET pattern)
5:04 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Hess's Law. Can you find a reaction's heat without ever doing it?
